name: Economic progressivism
summary: Economic progressivism holds that lightly regulated capitalism favors big business and the wealthy, and that government should correct this through progressive taxes, antitrust and regulation, labor protections, a minimum wage, universal health care and a broad welfare state. It keeps a market economy but treats property as subject to the public welfare, and it aims at upward mobility and less inequality. It is an economic program, so it takes few stated positions on cultural, religious or foreign-policy questions.
scope: The name 'economic progressivism' as the English Wikipedia article uses it: a left-of-centre economic philosophy joining social-democratic and political-progressive principles (regulated markets, progressive taxation, welfare state, labor rights). No encyclopedia, dictionary or scholarly work found names the term itself or ties any text, thinker or programme to it, so this pass treats the record as having no defining source: Theodore Roosevelt's 1910 New Nationalism speech, Franklin Roosevelt's 1944 economic bill of rights and the Congressional Progressive Caucus's agenda belong to the American progressive tradition, but nothing found ties them to this name.
